headline: PHIVOLCS Warns of Possible Lahars from Pinatubo and Taal Amid Heavy Habagat Rains
seoTitle: PHIVOLCS Warns of Pinatubo, Taal Lahars | FMB News
seoDescription: PHIVOLCS warned that prolonged Habagat rains could trigger lahars, muddy streamflows and volcanic debris flows around Pinatubo and Taal on August 29.
deck: Saturated volcanic deposits may be remobilized into river channels and downstream communities as heavy monsoon rain continues.
author: FMB News Desk

sections.heading: What happened
paragraphs: PHIVOLCS warned Saturday that prolonged and intense southwest-monsoon rainfall could generate lahars, muddy streamflows and volcanic debris flows around Mount Pinatubo and Taal Volcano.
The warning concerns rain-driven remobilization of old volcanic deposits and does not indicate a new eruption.

sections.heading: Pinatubo channels at risk
paragraphs: PHIVOLCS said non-eruption lahars may occur along the upper to middle reaches of the Sto. Tomas-Marella and Bucao river systems and could transition into muddy streamflows and floods downstream, potentially affecting San Marcelino, San Narciso, San Felipe and Botolan in Zambales.
Muddy streamflows may also develop along the O'Donnell and Pasig-Potrero river systems, affecting downstream communities in Tarlac and Pampanga.

sections.heading: Taal risk areas
paragraphs: Around Taal Volcano, saturated loose deposits may be remobilized on slopes west and north of Taal Lake. PHIVOLCS identified Agoncillo, Laurel and Talisay in Batangas among communities where muddy or debris flows could recur.

sections.heading: Context
paragraphs: Lahars can occur without an eruption when intense rain mobilizes loose ash, pyroclastic material and other volcanic sediment. Pinatubo watersheds still contain deposits from the 1991 eruption.

sections.heading: Why this matters
paragraphs: Rain-driven volcanic sediment flows can move through river and drainage systems into downstream communities, so the advisory is a separate hazard from ordinary surface flooding even though both are triggered by heavy rain.

sections.heading: What to watch next
paragraphs: PHIVOLCS urged local governments and communities in identified areas to monitor weather conditions and take preemptive safety measures as heavy rainfall continues.
